question.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{y}$ is enclosed between the line $x=y$ and the curve  $x=\frac{4}{y}$  for $1\le y\le 2.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type II plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121640/assets/163575c9a1adc54e1ccda5c3008e69413c44015596146bb435a528c4159abaa9.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,y\le x\le \frac{4}{y},\,1\le y\le 2}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{y}^{4/y}\frac{x}{y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}[{\int }_{y}^{4/y}x\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=y}^{x=4/y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}[\frac{8}{{y}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{8}{{y}^{3}}-\frac{y}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{4}{{y}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}]}_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & =[-1-1]-[-4-\frac{1}{4}] \\  & =\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
